stages.name: compatibility
stages.evidence: Pinned Xray 26.10.10 rejects public-IP Trojan security=none (exit 23); loopback accepted (exit 0). No live configuration changed.

stages.name: profiles_and_drivers
stages.evidence: 24 mandatory PostgreSQL/race/native regressions passed; legacy credentials and native listeners adopted without POST, applied ports remain reserved.

stages.name: unified_ui
stages.evidence: Browser regression passed: common New, all four protocols, plain Trojan public restriction, port 9443/500/automatic, existing Reality controls.

stages.name: regression_and_canary
stages.evidence: 17 isolated real core URI round trips and 16 native Sanaei create/port-change/fresh-verify lifecycles passed; actual active-core traffic proof handles API-hot-added listeners; SS Client-model mapping fixed.

stages.name: release_and_rollout
stages.evidence: Release 3bb0417 installed on both hosts; source 4a5041c; five readiness checks per host, matching running binary hashes, 600 existing Reality pins and existing credentials/policies preserved.

stages.name: production_output_and_control_progress
stages.evidence: Seven repeated ready observations; scheduler advanced throughout bulk recovery backlog. Final two Trojan profiles each verified 73/73. General and shared output covered all 73 healthy servers; country and connection mismatches zero.

constraints: Preserve credentials and existing Reality pins
No TLS stripping from TLS listeners
Keep cleanup, ownership, fresh route proof and output scope fences

release_gate_findings.finding: Worker supervision policy and role inventory lacked new profile modules
release_gate_findings.result: Publication blocked before production change; policies and role regression updated

release_gate_findings.finding: Primary installer retention guard rejected migration 184 legacy enabled-flag delegation; transaction and binaries rolled back automatically
release_gate_findings.result: Primary ready on prior 26c2dc5. Added version-specific complete-copy verification for policy, ownership, credential references and output revisions; migration checksum remains unchanged; missing copies are rejected in production-preserving regression.

release_gate_findings.finding: Runtime probe falsely blocked healthy Residential Trojan clients by requesting example.com, intentionally denied by route policy.
release_gate_findings.result: Probe destinations now follow explicit client class, not array position. Real native authenticated proof passed both classes; TLS and routing restrictions preserved.

release_gate_findings.finding: Native profile reconciliation held the shared writer during read-only authenticated traffic verification; a pending Reality client creation could be delayed by the fleet queue.
release_gate_findings.result: SENT recovery is observation-only without the shared writer; successful native writes release it before traffic proof while retaining the panel lock. Database regression checks writes retain ownership, proofs release it, and uncertain writes recover under an unrelated writer without another POST.

release_gate_findings.finding: Two fleet profiles require roughly 150 authenticated verifications; measured proofs averaged 9-12 seconds, exceeding the five-minute freshness budget with four lanes.
release_gate_findings.result: Eight supervised verification lanes share the existing ten-slot panel budget. Creation remains capped at two and native writes remain globally serialized. Freshness checks are unchanged.

release_gate_findings.finding: Post-rollout readiness exposed an older control-plane convoy: scheduler and billing waited behind the single bulk recovery lane; scheduler progress exceeded five minutes despite healthy panel output.
release_gate_findings.result: Scheduler gets an independent admission class under the unchanged five-operation parent; billing uses bounded provider-observation capacity. Account/capacity locks unchanged. Saturated-lane and actual 24-connection PostgreSQL pool regressions are required for publication.

release_gate_findings.finding: Final control scheduler qualification initially exceeded zero-wait SQL headroom with six simultaneous owners.
release_gate_findings.result: Rejected before publication; retained the original five-operation and 24-connection limits, with separate scheduler admission. Worst admitted PostgreSQL pool regression passed with zero wait/leak.

limitations: Current official pinned Xray rejects plaintext Trojan to public IPs. Public Trojan profiles use TLS; private-only plain capability is explicitly unavailable for this public fleet.
New independent profile credentials follow server lifetime and have no per-client quota or expiry. Existing Reality quotas, expiries and rotation remain under their preserved controller.
Protocol and credential membership are immutable after profile creation; port, compatible transport, name, server scope and enabled state remain editable.
Drivers are compiled, reviewed modules, not arbitrary executable uploads.

Live counts change during provisioning/expiry. Legacy VLESS class-specific output was 70/73 Direct and 69/73 Residential in the final snapshot while automatic capacity fill continued; general VLESS output covered 73/73, and both Trojan profiles covered every class on 73/73.
Provider/network outages can cause real verification failures and temporary withholding; automated retries and regression gates reduce recurrence but cannot guarantee zero future outages.

Primary disk reserve is tight. Installer preflight safely blocked two attempts before service changes; only reproducible build copies/caches were reclaimed. Database/configuration backups were preserved.
